metadata.title: Análisis del sentido espacial en estudiantes de secundaria en actividades PISA
metadata.venue: AIEM - Avances de investigación en educación matemática

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2012 released items (space and shape) and collects student responses from 122 15-year-old students in first-year Uruguayan high school (bachillerato) in a single private institution in Montevideo. The analysis is based on didactic content analysis and then correlational/regression analyses between coded spatial-sense indicators and teachers’ classroom-test grades; the manuscript does not report the use of PISA sampling weights or any complex-survey design weights. Because the dependent variable is a classroom-test grade and the predictors are binary-coded manifestations of spatial-sense components derived from students’ written solutions, standard PISA PV-based weighting procedures are not described. Consequently, readers should treat the results as descriptive/associational for this local sample rather than as population-representative estimates for Uruguay.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The study does not model PISA cognitive achievement scores generated via Plausible Values; instead, it codes students’ manifestations of spatial-sense components from responses to selected PISA 2012 tasks and relates these indicators to teachers’ classroom-test grades. Because the dependent variable is not a PV-based achievement scale, PV handling is not applicable. The manuscript also does not describe any missing-data rule for the coded indicators or the classroom grades, so missing-data handling is not reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The study selects eight released PISA 2012 activities in the content domain space and shape (excluding interactive tasks due to inaccessible links). For the classroom component, it targets first-year bachillerato because it contains most 15-year-olds (PISA age group). Data collection uses two questionnaire sessions plus a geometry classroom test administered in 2022 by four teachers at a private school in Montevideo; students are included only if they attend the geometry test and both questionnaire sessions. The final analytic sample comprises 122 students (E1–E122) who meet these attendance criteria.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that This descriptive didactic study analyzes spatial sense in secondary students using selected PISA 2012 released tasks from the space and shape domain and compares coded spatial-sense manifestations with teachers’ classroom-test performance. The analytic sample is 122 Uruguayan 15-year-olds in first-year bachillerato from a single private school in Montevideo. The authors operationalize spatial sense through two sets of indicators: management of geometric concepts and visualization skills, coded as binary manifestations across 13 PISA questions (with sums such as H2_C and H2_H) and then relate these indicators to the teachers’ grades (“nota”). Using correlation analyses, they find statistically significant positive associations between teachers’ performance and multiple spatial-sense indicators (e.g., note correlates with several concept-management and visualization variables). They further run regression analyses and report that performance is significantly predicted (p<.05) only by one concept-management variable and one visualization variable, specifically linked to question H2. Limitations include the local, single-institution sample and the absence of reported missing-data rules and any PV/weighting strategy. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This paper is not an empirical machine-learning/predictive modeling study: it uses didactic content analysis plus correlation and regression to examine associations between coded spatial-sense components and teachers’ classroom grades. Therefore, no ML algorithms, PV handling, or ML performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) are applicable, and main_findings are intentionally left empty per the schema rules for non-ML empirical designs.
